report.headline: Usage projected to shrink further in the NBA move, while the shooting-efficiency projection carries no real signal

projection.text: Projected usage rate falls to 12.6% in the NBA, down from 15.6% in the EuroLeague, landing roughly 1.4 standard deviations below the league-average usage rate of 20.1% (SD 5.4%).

risks.text: Usage was already 0.97 standard deviations below the EuroLeague average in the source season, and the projected NBA usage of 12.6% sits about 1.4 standard deviations below the NBA average of 20.1% (SD 5.4%), pointing to a marginal offensive role at best.

The prediction intervals for usage are wide -- 7.1% to 18.0% at 80%, 4.3% to 20.9% at 95% -- covering everything from a fringe bench role to a near-average rotation usage rate, so the point estimate should not be read as precise.

The true shooting projection of 53.5% is not trustworthy: the model's error (4.7 percentage points) is identical to the error of simply guessing the NBA league average, so no efficiency signal should be drawn from it.

The underlying estimate rests on only 61 historical EL->NBA transitions, and the subject was already 27 years old in the source season, limiting how much upside beyond the projection should be assumed.

strengths.text: Three-point reliance was heavy in the EuroLeague, with 44.9% of field-goal attempts coming from beyond the arc, a profile consistent with a lower-usage floor-spacing role.
Turnover rate was modest at 13.3% alongside some secondary playmaking (9.7% assist rate, 2.235 assists per 75), suggesting secure ball-handling in a complementary role.
Rebounding production was solid for a perimeter-oriented player, at 5.625 rebounds per 75 possessions.

uncertainty.text: The 80% prediction interval for usage, 7.1% to 18.0%, spans roughly two standard deviations of the NBA usage distribution (SD 5.4%), meaning the model can rank this kind of transition but cannot pin an individual outcome; the true shooting projection of 53.5% should be treated as carrying no information at all, since its out-of-fold error (4.7 points) is no better than a naive league-average guess (4.7 points).
